newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. navy plane with four crew missing off Israel.
newsitem.headline: U.S. navy plane with four crew missing off Israel.

text.p: A U.S. navy plane with four crew went missing on Tuesday night while on a training exercise off Israel, the United States said on Wednesday.
U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk told Israel's Channel One Television the plane was on a joint exercise with an Israeli submarine and now appeared to be lost in the Mediterranean Sea.

"The aircraft, with four crew members aboard, was conducting a routine training exercise off the coast of Israel when it disappeared from radar at 19.56 local (1756 GMT)," said a U.S. Information Service statement, quoting the U.S. Sixth Fleet.

It said rescue crews were searching the sea for the S-3B Viking, a fixed-wing carrier-based anti-submarine aircraft, which disappeared about 140 kms (90 miles) west of Haifa after taking off from the aircraft carrier Theodore Roosevelt.
The statement said the plane was assigned to the Naval Air Station Cecil Field in Jacksonville, Florida.

The plane went missing about the same time as 73 Israeli soldiers were killed in a mid-air crash of two U.S.-made Sikorsky CH-53 helicopters, the biggest military air disaster in Israel's 49-year-old history.
"I think it just underscores the way in which working together to prepare for war and to fight for peace we face the same dangers and unfortunately the same tragedies," Indyk said.
